props.title: Dial in a pour-over
props.intro: Practise adjusting one variable at a time, with less help at each level.

toolbox.label: Brew ratio chart
toolbox.text: Check the target ratio before you change anything.

toolbox.label: Taste wheel
toolbox.text: Name what you taste before deciding what to fix.

challenges.prompt: The cup tastes sour and thin. Which single change should you try first?

hints.text: Sour usually means under-extraction; you want more extraction, not less.
What does sourness tell you about how much was dissolved?
Look at the grind and temperature rows of the troubleshooting chart.

options.label: Grind finer
options.feedback: A finer grind exposes more surface, so more dissolves and the sourness fades.

options.label: Use cooler water
options.feedback: Cooler water dissolves less, which makes under-extraction worse.

challenges.workedSolution: Sour and thin points to under-extraction. Change one variable: grind one step finer and brew again. Cooler water would extract even less.

challenges.prompt: Write the adjustment plan for a bitter, dry cup, in your own words.

hints.text: Bitter and dry is the opposite problem of sour.

challenges.workedSolution: Bitter and dry means over-extraction: grind one step coarser or shorten the brew time, change only one, and taste again.
